extractor.note: Read every paragraph carrying transcend- (outside transcendental), immanen- or overstep, in file order. No stratum is set: the commentary does not assign its sections to the Paris lectures, the 1929 Meditations or the 1931 French text.

coverage_note: Term-led pass over the whole file (lines 1-438): every paragraph containing the transcendence family, including bare transcendent and immanent, was read; paragraphs without such a word were not read.

units.claim: Transcendence, the correlate-concept of the transcendental, belongs to the very sense of everything worldly, though the world draws all its sense and validity from my experiencing.
units.quote: To the very sense of everything worldly belongs this transcendence, although it acquires and can only acquire the entire sense that determines it, together with its being-validity, from my experiencing

units.claim: If this transcendence of unreal containedness belongs to the sense of the world, the ego that carries the world as valid sense is called transcendental.
units.quote: If this transcendence of unreal containedness belongs to the very sense of the world, then the ego itself, which carries the world as a valid sense and which is itself necessarily presupposed by the world, is called transcendental in the phenomenological sense

units.claim: The ego cogito is not to be used as a premise for inferences to a transcendent subjectivity; the epoché instead discloses a novel sphere of transcendental experience.
units.quote: instead of wishing to use the ego cogito as an apodictically evident premise for supposedly necessary inferences to a transcendent subjectivity

units.claim: Every object whatsoever, including every immanent one, designates a rule-structure of the transcendental ego.
units.quote: Every object, every object whatsoever (including every immanent one), designates a rule-structure of the transcendental ego.

units.claim: Existing objects for the ego include both objects in its adequately verifiable immanent time-sphere and world-objects demonstrated in merely presumptive external experience.
units.quote: not only objects in its adequately verifiable immanent time-sphere but also the world-objects demonstrated as existing in the concordance of the course of inadequate, merely presumptive external experience

units.claim: The problem of the traditional theory of knowledge, as which phenomenology may also characterize itself, is that of transcendence, the clarification of the principled possibility of cognition.
units.quote: The problem of the traditional theory of knowledge is that of transcendence. It wishes to clarify the principled possibility of cognition.

units.claim: Transcendence in every form is an immanent being-character constituting itself within the ego, and every sense and being, immanent or transcendent, falls within transcendental subjectivity.
units.quote: Transcendence in every form is an immanent being-character constituting itself within the ego.

units.claim: The ego's own extends to transcendent objects of outer sensibility insofar as they are originally constituted through its own sensibility and apperceptions.
units.quote: This includes transcendent objects of outer sensibility, insofar as they are actually originally constituted through my own sensibility, my own apperceptions, as concretely inseparable from them.

units.claim: What is to be made understandable is how the sense-giving of objective transcendence comes about at a higher founded level, as static analysis rather than genesis.
units.quote: What is now to be made understandable is how, at the higher founded level, the sense-giving of objective transcendence comes about — and this as experience, not as the disclosure of a temporally progressing genesis but as a static analysis.

units.claim: Foreign body and foreign governing ego are given in the manner of a unitary transcending experience.
units.quote: In this interweaving, foreign body and foreign governing ego are given in the manner of a unitary transcending experience.

absences.expected_because: The section sets aside problems of the range of transcendental cognition, which §40 identifies with the traditional problem of transcendence.
